findings.title: Rejected device is admitted on its next request
findings.description:
`tagDeviceUI` marks the device in the local cache (impl.go:87) before calling `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (impl.go:93). When the limit is hit, the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, `TagDevice` returns it (impl.go:147), and `Authenticate` rejects the request (client.go:45-47). The cache entry is not removed, and it lasts 29 minutes (impl.go:42).

The next request from the same device hits the cache check at impl.go:83-85, `tagDeviceUI` returns nil, and the request is admitted. After expiry the cycle repeats, so a rejected device gets in on alternating attempts for as long as the limit holds.

Fix: call `SetDefault` only after the store write succeeds, or delete the key on error. The same ordering also means a failed write (a transient DB error, or a cancelled request context, which client.go now passes through) suppresses tagging for 29 minutes. The existing `localCacheSafety` test only covers a pre-populated cache hit, so it does not catch this.

findings.title: Count-then-write is not atomic, so the limit can be overshot
findings.description:
`CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` (line 110) and then the insert or `updateDevice` as separate statements, with no transaction or conditional insert. Concurrent logins from new device IDs that all see `count = limit-1` will all insert. The overshoot is bounded by concurrency, but the setting reads as a hard cap.

Either document it as a soft limit, or do the check and insert in one transaction (`WithTransactionalDbSession`) or a single conditional `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < ?`.

findings.title: Tagging moved from a background goroutine into the login request path
findings.description:
Before this change, tagging ran in a goroutine with its own context, a 2-minute timeout (`timeoutTag`), and a `recover()`. Now `Authenticate` waits on `TagDevice` using the request context. Every cache-miss anonymous request performs a write on the request path, and with `device_limit > 0` a `COUNT(*)` first. That adds DB latency and DB-failure exposure to every anonymous page load, including the default `device_limit = 0`, where the result is only logged.

The count is index-backed (`anonservice/migrations.go:24`), so the cost is bounded, but the synchronous write is only needed when a limit is configured. Consider keeping tagging best-effort and async when `deviceLimit == 0`, and synchronous only when a limit is set. The diff also drops the explicit timeout and the panic recovery without mentioning either.

findings.title: Retried closure mutates captured `args`, so lock retries send a malformed statement
findings.description:
`withDbSession` re-invokes the callback when SQLite returns `SQLITE_BUSY` or `SQLITE_LOCKED` (`pkg/services/sqlstore/session.go:86-103`, retried via `retryer.Retry` at line 127). The closure runs `args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)`, which rewrites the captured `args`. On the first retry the slice already starts with the query text, so `Exec` receives the SQL twice and the retry fails.

Build a local slice inside the closure (`execArgs := append([]any{query}, args...)`). The same pattern exists in `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (database.go:150). That predates this change but has the same bug. The new function also uses `[]interface{}` where the rest of the file uses `[]any`.

findings.title: Device limit can be bypassed by omitting the device header
findings.description:
`TagDevice` returns nil when `X-Grafana-Device-Id` is absent (impl.go:119-122), and `Authenticate` admits the request. Requests without the header are never counted or limited. New random IDs are rejected once the limit is reached, but a client can skip the header and avoid the check entirely.

If the limit is meant to cap anonymous access, this is a gap. If it only caps tracked devices, document that, because operators will otherwise assume the setting caps access.

findings.title: Three definitions of the same 30-day window
findings.description: `impl.go` still defines `thirtyDays` (line 25), used by `usageStatFn`. The diff adds `anonymousDeviceExpiration` in `api/api.go:18` and again in `anonstore/database.go:16`. The same value now has two names, and one constant is defined in two packages. Export one constant from `anonstore` and use it in all three places.

findings.title: `ProvideAnonDBStore` wire registration is now stale
findings.description:
The service now builds its own store from `db.DB` (impl.go:43), so nothing consumes the `anonstore.AnonStore` binding at wire.go:375. The new `ProvideAnonDBStore(db, int64)` signature also can't be injected, since wire has no provider for a bare int64.

Remove the provider and bind, or keep the store injected and pass the limit another way. The service can no longer receive an `AnonStore` from DI, which is why `impl_test.go` changed to build a real DB. I could not verify wire generation because `pkg/server/wire_gen.go` is not in this checkout.

findings.title: `anonymousDeviceLimit` is typed `undefined` in the runtime class
findings.description:
The interface declares `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` (packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200), but the class initializer `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` has no annotation. With `strict: true` in tsconfig, the inferred type is `undefined`, so `config.anonymousDeviceLimit` on `GrafanaBootConfig` cannot be compared to a number. The file's convention is annotated, for example `loginError: string | undefined = undefined;` at line 85.

The backend always sends an int64 (default 0), so `number` is the accurate contract. Suggested fix: `anonymousDeviceLimit: number = 0;` in the class, and `anonymousDeviceLimit: number;` in the interface. I have not compiled this.

findings.title: `device_limit` is undocumented
findings.description: `device_limit` is read in `pkg/setting/setting.go:1654`, but it is not added to `conf/defaults.ini` or `conf/sample.ini` next to `hide_version`, and the authentication docs do not mention it. Operators cannot discover the key, that 0 means unlimited, or that exceeding the limit rejects anonymous logins.

findings.title: Tests miss the paths that matter for the limit
findings.description:
`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` covers only the rejection branch. Not covered:
- (a) an existing active device is still admitted at the limit. This is the `updateDevice` success path, which the `BETWEEN` window exists for.
- (b) a device whose `updated_at` is older than 30 days is rejected at the limit.
- (c) `Authenticate` returning `ErrDeviceLimitReached` (client.go:45-47), and the non-limit error path continuing to admit the request.
- (d) a rejected device retried, which would have caught the cache bug above.
- (e) `device_limit` parsing in `setting.go:1654`.

findings.title: Doc comment describes parameters that don't exist
findings.description: The comment on `updateDevice` says "has been updated between the given times", but the function takes no times. The window is fixed relative to `device.UpdatedAt`. The function also mixes policy into the store layer, returning `ErrDeviceLimitReached` for both unknown and inactive devices. Fix the comment to describe the actual window.

findings.title: Rejected logins are logged at Warn on every request
findings.description: Once the limit is reached, each rejected anonymous request returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. `authenticate` logs it through `errorLogFunc` (service.go:230, which defaults to Warn at line 364) and `Authenticate` increments `failedAuth` (service.go:220). A persistent limit condition will flood logs at Warn. Consider a Debug log or a dedicated metric.

findings.title: `ErrDeviceLimitReached` should use `errors.New`
findings.description: `fmt.Errorf` with no format verbs is equivalent to `errors.New`, which is the usual idiom for sentinel errors. Trivial.

findings.title: MySQL `RowsAffected` check is correct
findings.description: The zero-rows check in `updateDevice` relies on `RowsAffected` counting matched rows. The MySQL DSN sets `clientFoundRows=true`, so an UPDATE that rewrites identical values still reports matched rows and is not mistaken for a limit rejection.
